[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07.md#abb-context]

### ABB Context

- **Parent L2 Capability**: Application Security Testing — [GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02](../GUID-SEC-APP-CAP-DESC-1.7.02.md)
- **ABB Catalog**: [GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06](../GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06.md)
- **Capability Statement**: The enterprise SHALL have an architectural capability to perform automated analysis of application source code and compiled artifacts to identify security weaknesses before the application is executed.
page_texts.4:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07.md#abb-scope]

### ABB Scope

**In Scope**:
- Architectural capability to scan application source code for known vulnerability patterns at build or commit time
- Integration of scan results into pipeline gate decisions
- Triage and baseline management of identified findings

**Out of Scope**:
- Analysis of running application behavior (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-DAST-2.7.08)
- Analysis of third-party dependency components (see GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SCA-2.7.10)
- Security controls, tool selection, or configuration baselines (`standards/security/`)

[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07.md#core-principles]

### Core Principles

- SAST capability SHALL be integrated into the development pipeline at a point where results are available to developers before code is merged to a shared branch.
- Pipeline gate decisions SHOULD use finding severity and a defined exception process rather than blocking all findings unconditionally.
- Scan results SHALL be attributed to the authoring team and tracked over time to enable trending analysis.
- Suppression of findings MAY be permitted only through a documented, approved exception process.
page_texts.8:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07.md#source-code-analysis]

#### Source Code Analysis

**Architectural intent**: Identify security weaknesses in application source code using pattern-based and data-flow analysis without executing the code.

**Design guidance**:
- Analysis SHALL cover the primary application language(s) in use.
- The capability SHOULD support incremental analysis (scanning only changed code) to support pipeline performance requirements.
- Findings SHALL be classified using a consistent severity taxonomy.
page_texts.9:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07.md#pipeline-integration]

#### Pipeline Integration

**Architectural intent**: Surface SAST findings at the point in the development lifecycle where remediation cost is lowest.

**Design guidance**:
- SAST SHALL be invoked automatically on pull request creation or commit to a defined integration branch.
- The capability SHALL provide findings in a format consumable by the pipeline orchestration system.
- Results SHOULD be surfaced to developers in their development environment or pull request interface.
page_texts.10:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07.md#integration-interfaces]

### Integration Interfaces

| Interface | Direction | Consuming ABB | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| Pipeline Trigger | Inbound | CI/CD Pipeline | Receives code commit or PR event to initiate scan |
| Findings Output | Outbound | GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-CAT-2.7.06 | Structured findings consumed by gate logic and tracking systems |
| Developer Feedback | Outbound | Developer Tooling | Findings surfaced in IDE or PR review interface |
page_texts.11:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07.md#zero-trust-alignment-nist-sp-800-207]

### Zero Trust Alignment (NIST SP 800-207)

SAST advances the Applications and Workloads pillar by reducing the exploitable vulnerability surface of applications before they are deployed into any execution environment, trusted or otherwise. It directly supports the principle that workloads should be verified before being trusted with access to enterprise resources.
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07.md#nist-sp-800-53-intent-alignment]

### NIST SP 800-53 Intent Alignment

This ABB enables the architectural intent of the SA (System and Services Acquisition) family — specifically the intent that security engineering principles are applied to the system development lifecycle — and the SI (System and Information Integrity) family, which addresses the identification and remediation of security flaws.
page_texts.13:
[strategy/guidance/security/Application/abbs/GUID-SEC-APP-ABB-SAST-2.7.07.md#constraints-and-dependencies]

### Constraints and Dependencies

- Effectiveness depends on language support coverage of the selected analysis capability; architecture decisions must account for polyglot application portfolios.
- SAST is one layer of a defense-in-depth testing posture and SHALL NOT be treated as a substitute for dynamic or interactive analysis.
- False positive rates must be managed to preserve developer trust in the capability.
